newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian debt rally rubs off on NZ at close.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt rally rubs off on NZ at close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
New Zealand debt markets got a powerful shot in the arm on Friday as enthusiasm for Australian paper flowed through to the local market right across the curve.
Australian debt markets had rallied sharply after weak retail trade data fuelled speculation that the Australian Reserve Bank may ease monetary policy again.
The sharp movement in Australian markets was enough to outweigh weakness in the New Zealand dollar, which fell to US$0.6890/00 from 0.6900/07 at Thursday's close.
The Trade-Weighted Index was again ending near its lows and the Monetary Conditions Index deteriorated to minus 0.86 from minus 0.76.
The market had started on a positive note as local rates realigned themselves after a strong close in U.S. Treasuries.
"It then just followed the pace set by Australia. They just kept on charging and we kept on playing catchup," a dealer said.
"No domestic influence was going to cause that."
In the long end, November 2006 bonds rallied about 10 basis points to close at 7.45 while in the short end, key 90-day bank bills ended at 7.07 percent from 7.16.
